news.summary_en: Intelligence firm Strider Technologies identified that Alice Huang and her associates built a complex network utilizing $3.6 billion in Chinese government funding for data centers equipped with Nvidia AI chips. The investigation reveals that these entities maintain deep ties to Chinese military contractors and the Ministry of State Security, posing significant compliance risks regarding the diversion of restricted hardware into military research.
paragraphs: Alice Huang, the woman at the center of the Nvidia scandal, has extensive ties through her family and associates to China’s defense industry, according to an independent research firm and corporate filings reviewed by The New York Times.

The findings show a web of relationships, most of them indirect, linking Ms. Huang’s family and companies that acquired Nvidia chips to Chinese state-owned defense contractors that supply the People’s Liberation Army.

The nature of those relationships, including the vital question of whether Nvidia chips ended up being used to support Chinese military projects, remains murky. But the revelations, along with an investigation by The Times published on Wednesday, underscore how the Chinese effort to acquire access to the computing power of Nvidia’s chips is intertwined with Beijing’s desire to harness artificial intelligence to bolster its military capabilities.

That outcome has long been feared by U.S. national security officials, given that the technology could help China develop more sophisticated weapons, carry out cyberattacks and integrate A.I. into the battlefield.

A confidential analysis by Strider Technologies, an independent intelligence firm that employs former intelligence officers and experts on China and specializes in corporate intelligence, shows that about $3.6 billion in Chinese government money flowed through companies associated with Ms. Huang’s family or associates. The government money funded technology projects, including data centers that received Nvidia chips.
The New York Times reviewed the Strider findings. Many of the corporate ties revealed by Strider were independently confirmed by The Times.

The Times reported last month that U.S. officials believe Ms. Huang, a Chinese citizen also known as Huang Le, is a Chinese intelligence asset who was providing information to the Ministry of State Security. The Strider Technologies analysis and the review of corporate filings by The Times show that she; her sister, Huang Yu; and an investor named Kang Wei, who was Alice Huang’s business partner and often introduced as her husband, are tied to a web of companies that connect official Nvidia partners, which can buy advanced Nvidia A.I. chips, to state- and military-linked projects.
Nvidia’s co-founder, Jensen Huang, stepped down as the company’s chief executive after acknowledging an affair with Alice Huang, who is no relation.

Companies in the Huang family’s network co-own a cybersecurity venture with an arm of China’s main military-electronics conglomerate, lease Nvidia-powered servers financed by an affiliate of its largest military aircraft maker and in one case share a parent company with a maker of radar and missile components.

Two companies that have partnerships with Nvidia, Megaspeed and Century Litong, are connected to Ms. Huang. Ms. Huang ran Megaspeed, a Singapore-based data center firm that is under investigation by the Justice Department for smuggling advanced chips into China. Megaspeed has said Ms. Huang, whose involvement with Mr. Huang corresponded with a period when it was acquiring large numbers of Nvidia chips, no longer works for the company.

Ms. Huang’s family members had prominent roles and significant investments in the data center firm that founded Century Litong, which is based in Shanghai and rents out computing power to major Chinese companies and military contractors. The family members include Ms. Huang’s sister and Mr. Kang.

U.S. officials are also working to learn more about Ms. Huang and her efforts to help supply chips to data centers. The nature and extent of her ties to the P.L.A. and the companies it controls are a focus of that work, according to people briefed on the American efforts.

The ties are complex and often indirect. The research does not show whether the P.L.A. used computing power in the data centers that the family’s companies helped build. But it shows how deeply Ms. Huang and her family are intertwined with the Chinese state, and the inextricable connections between China’s tech industry and its military.

“Beijing has spent years building these networks that reach deep into Western economies,” said Greg Levesque, the chief executive of Strider. “Follow the money and, too often, you find the P.L.A. at the end of it.”

Mr. Levesque said China was exploiting more Western technology, capital and talent than ever before to build its defense industrial base. “This is happening on a scale we simply weren’t seeing a few years ago,” he said.
Nvidia declined to comment. Megaspeed did not respond to a request for comment. Ms. Huang could not be reached for comment.

From late last year into early this year, Century Litong appears to have been one of only a few sources able to supply Nvidia chips to China at the vast scale needed for its A.I. build-out, according to Strider.

Those chips were key to building the data centers that drive China’s A.I. development. Investigators are trying to determine how many of the chips that were used in those data centers were banned under U.S. export controls and, in essence, smuggled into the country. Companies controlled by Ms. Huang and her relatives were instrumental in supplying the chips, Strider found.
“Essentially, those entities worked around the controls to continue to meet the chip demands of the customers they already had, including at new data centers,” Mr. Levesque said.

On Thursday, the House Foreign Affairs Committee took the unusual step of releasing confidential information on Nvidia’s license applications to legally sell H200 chips to Chinese firms. The list showed that Nvidia had sought permission to sell more than 40,000 H200s to the Hong Kong subsidiary of Century Litong.
An Nvidia spokesman said that, despite receiving some licenses, it had already stopped shipping H200s to China, and Nvidia had not and would not ship to that firm.

Century Litong has said it has no business dealings with Ms. Huang. But the company was founded in 2023 by Century Longteng, a data center operator that was then 27 percent owned by an investment firm controlled by Ms. Huang’s sister. Mr. Kang, Ms. Huang’s presumed husband, had been Century Longteng’s executive director since February 2022, according to Strider.

In 2023, Jiangsu Lettall Electronic, a Shanghai-listed maker of metal parts for flat-screen TVs, bought 90 percent of Century Litong, and owned all of it by 2024. Lettall also owns 80 percent of Nanjing Jinning Microwave, a maker of components that Lettall has said are used in Chinese radar and missile systems. Strider said Jinning’s parts go into the P.L.A.’s DF-series missiles, including intercontinental ballistic missiles and anti-ship “carrier killers,” as well as the J-20 stealth fighter plane.
China’s defense industry wants advanced A.I. chips to design better missiles and build other military software, experts have said.

Lettall did not respond to an emailed request for comment. Asked about Ms. Huang’s network of companies and their efforts to acquire chips, the spokesman for the Chinese Embassy in Washington said he was not familiar with the situation. “We have made clear more than once our principled position on U.S. chip exports to China,” said the spokesman, Liu Chang.

Century Litong delivered servers containing Nvidia’s H800 chips to a supercomputing center in Shanghai in October 2023, according to Strider. It is unclear where Century Litong obtained those chips, but they may have been obtained legally, since U.S. restrictions on the sale of the H800 to China did not go into effect until that same month.

Century Litong now runs servers at the Shanghai supercomputing center under a lease of about $54 million from a leasing arm of the Aviation Industry Corporation of China, China’s state aerospace and defense conglomerate.

Century Litong’s reach extends far beyond the Chinese A.I. giant Tencent. When Lettall bought into the company in 2023, it said all of Century Litong’s computing business would be housed in two places: the Tencent center in Shanghai and a data center in Shenzhen.

The Shenzhen center was built for the cloud unit of Huawei, the Chinese telecom giant that has long been under sanctions by the United States over national security concerns. Huawei awarded the project in 2022 to a company controlled by Century Longteng, according to corporate filings.

Century Litong’s customers have also included a unit of China Electronics Technology Group, or C.E.T.C., a state-owned military electronics maker. The United States has included C.E.T.C. on its list of companies that it publicly identifies as doing work with the Chinese military, banning the firm from doing work with Pentagon suppliers.
Another Century Litong partner is Hangjin Technology, a listed company whose subsidiaries make chips for China’s military.

Until last December, Hangjin controlled Chaoqing, an Nvidia partner whose website once listed High-Flyer, the hedge fund behind the Chinese A.I. start-up DeepSeek, as a partner. Others on the list included the military-linked Zhejiang Lab and its co-founder, Alibaba.

DeepSeek has attracted attention for its cutting-edge A.I. models. But lawmakers in the United States have also accused it of presenting national security risks, and the federal government has banned employees from using it. news.title: The most misunderstood graph in AI just got a major update
news.title_en: The most misunderstood graph in AI just got a major update
news.author: Grace Huckins
news.content_snippet:
A new report from the AI evaluation nonprofit METR finds that some AI capabilities are continuing to improve along an exponential trajectory—but it also indicates that models aren’t quite as good at tasks that require judgment as they are at coding.

The report is an update to the organization’s time horizon plot, which was widely shared— and widely misinterpreted , due to the complexity of the measures it used. METR evaluated models by having them attempt a large suite of tasks, each of which h
news.summary_en: Nonprofit evaluation group METR has updated its time-horizon plot for AI capabilities, indicating that models show exponential growth in verifiable tasks like coding and mathematics, but lag in judgment-based tasks that lack automated verification. The report highlights the technological bottleneck in applying reinforcement learning to complex, open-ended research decisions, a capability critical for future autonomous R&D.
paragraphs: A new report from the AI evaluation nonprofit METR finds that some AI capabilities are continuing to improve along an exponential trajectory—but it also indicates that models aren’t quite as good at tasks that require judgment as they are at coding.

The report is an update to the organization’s time horizon plot, which was widely shared— and widely misinterpreted , due to the complexity of the measures it used. METR evaluated models by having them attempt a large suite of tasks, each of which had also been completed by humans. Each task’s difficulty was scored by how long it took the human testers to finish it—and then models were rated according to the length of the tasks that they could complete. That plot showed that AI systems were rapidly improving—every four months, the length of the tasks that frontier models could successfully complete doubled.

The updated plot adds more tasks—some that are estimated to take humans far longer than the tasks in the original suite, and others that are more open-ended. One of the biggest questions in AI right now is the extent to which progress on “verifiable” tasks—where it’s possible to check automatically whether an AI system has succeeded or failed—carry over into tasks on which success or failure is harder to measure. We know how to teach neural networks how to do verifiable tasks: Researchers have the systems attempt the task many times, strengthen the neural pathways that contribute to success, and weaken the pathways that contribute to failures. That’s why AI systems have become so good at coding and math, two domains where it’s possible to determine automatically whether a solution does or doesn’t work.

It’s much harder to apply this technique, known as reinforcement learning, to tasks where success is less well defined or takes longer to ascertain—such as choosing a new research direction. For the same reason, it’s tough to evaluate AI performance on these tasks, so METR’s original time horizon plot didn’t include any of them. But it’s precisely this type of task that will prove essential to AI systems automating research and development.

And AI research and development is an especially hot topic right now. Parts of the AI community are still reeling from a different, heavily redacted METR report from earlier this month weeks ago, which claimed that AI might be speeding up the pace of AI capabilities progress at Anthropic by a factor of two. That report sparked fears that the company (which just had a blockbuster IPO) could soon achieve full recursive self-improvement, a regime in which AI systems autonomously design their own successors with no human involvement.

METR researchers have worked to incorporate some of these fuzzier, judgment-laden tasks that could be most relevant to AI research and development into their new suite. In one task, they ask models to design new AI evaluations that METR could use in its research and then have human METR employees score the results. Even though the most advanced models are now better than almost every human at software engineering, here they fall short: Not one of the AI-designed evaluations was good enough for METR employees to consider it useful for their research.

In another task, models have to score philosophical arguments. This task is intended to capture the extent to which models can exercise good judgment—though METR writes in the report that employees disagree about the extent to which the task is relevant for AI R&D automation. On this task, too, models fell short of human performance.

Though it’s difficult to score these new tasks—and even more so to determine what these scores mean—experts I spoke with appreciate that METR is incorporating new types of evaluations into their work. “We’re at the point where AI evaluations need to get more creative,” says Sayash Kapoor, a computer scientist and incoming professor at UC Berkeley. “Trying to push the envelope of the space of evaluations is a welcome change.”

Kapoor says he wasn’t surprised to see that models fall short of performance on more open-ended tasks, such as designing an AI evaluation—in a preprint from August , he and his collaborators reported that AI models are not yet able to reproduce human computer science research on their own. And in a Wednesday blog post, OpenAI reported that its models don’t do as well on the real-world tasks its employees ask them to do as they do on the easier, more verifiable tasks in METR’s original task suite.

Still, people disagree about how to interpret current performance differences on easily verifiable and hard-to-verify tasks, Kapoor says. Though he thinks that research taste—the ability to choose promising research questions, hypotheses, and experiments—will prove a major bottleneck to AI R&D automation, others contend that models trained on easy-to-verify tasks will eventually be able to successfully complete open-ended tasks as well. And progress on verifiable tasks doesn’t seem to be slowing down.

Even if the models do lag behind human performance on open-ended tasks right now, the new report suggests that they might be getting better. Some of the newest models, such as Opus 5.5, tend to achieve what METR calls “borderline above the bar” performance on the evaluation design tasks—not yet usable for METR’s research, but promising. Just a year ago, every model was scoring in the “clearly below the bar” category.

But because these open-ended and judgment-heavy tasks are so tough to design and score, METR includes few of them in its report, and that makes it difficult to predict whether and how models might continue to progress in these areas. “The improvement we observe, I think that does tell us something for the current moment,” says Najoung Kim, a linguist and computer scientist at Boston University. “I’m not sure just yet how to think about how it would extrapolate.”

Matt Putz, a member of the technical staff at METR, says that predicting progress on these kinds of tasks is likely to remain difficult. “By their nature, hard-to-verify or judgment-laden tasks are much harder to study, and especially to quantify,” he said in an email. “Ultimately, I don’t think we’ll be able to establish trends as clean and robust as for the easy-to-specify [tasks].”

In general, METR is clearly butting up against the practical difficulties of testing AI performance on difficult and underspecified tasks—precisely the tasks most relevant to AI R&D automation. METR’s time horizon plots score task difficulty by evaluating how long it would take a human to complete the task, and for the original plot they measured this quantity by actually having people try each task.

In the new report, however, the completion times are mostly estimates, because paying people to complete tasks that might take hundreds of hours, or that only a few experts are qualified to complete, is prohibitively expensive and time-consuming. Other tasks have more specific shortcomings—for example, for the philosophical argument task, just one person rated most of the arguments, and agents are judged by how well they agree with that particular individual. It’s possible that the scores would change if more experts were surveyed—but that, too, is time consuming.

It’s still early days for evaluating models on tasks that are hard to validate or require judgment. And while the experts I spoke with see the inclusion of these tasks in METR’s newest time horizon plot as a clear step in the right direction, they agree that we are still far from achieving any definitive answers about whether, and how quickly, automated AI R&D might be coming. “This move towards open-ended tasks is promising,” Kapoor says. But, he adds, “there is just such a lot more to be done to actually get a fuller understanding.”

谷歌最近发布了 Loop，这是其新的自我改进的人工智能代理，可以自主地实现给定的目标。

Loop 内部称为 Jitro；有趣的是，这就是 Jules v2 的确切名称。

1. 用户通过将其连接到选定的 Github
celebrity.full_text_en:
Google recently announced Loop, its new self-improving AI agent that can autonomously work toward a given goal. 

Loop is internally called Jitro; interestingly, that was the exact name for Jules v2. 

Here is how it works 👀

1. Users start creating a Workspace by connecting it to a selected Github project and adding basic information. 

2. Users can create loops manually or select ones that are already predefined (ex., Harden Application Security)

"Custom Loops" can be created via a prompt or by manually filling in the Loop title, icon, and objective. 

> "Loops are mid- to long-term objectives for Stitch Loop to continuously work toward. They can range from highly specific to broad, but should always be something code can achieve," says the description. 

3. Users can connect additional context in the form of Integrations, Files, Links, or additional repositories.

More than 100 integrations are available there, including services like Jira, Linear, Datadog, Sentry, Notion, Snowflake, Salesforce, Intercom, Discord, Slack, Figma, and many others. 

Custom MCPs are supported as well. 

4. After creating a workspace, Loop will start digging into your project details and generate its own Skills about the product and product metrics. 

These Skills will live in a separate tab and can be edited in the UI in Markdown. 

5. When the Workspace is ready, Loop will suggest metrics and goals based on its own research. Users can convert these suggestions into loops right away. 

When a Loop is created, it appears as a running process in the main UI. 

6. When a Loop is finished, users will see a list of suggestions for every loop, along with a number associated with a target metric and progress status. 

Example Loop:
- Goal - Scale Telegram community contributions.
- KPIs - community members, registered contributors, active members. 

A high-level goal would be broken down into sub-KPIs. When users open a dedicated Loop page, all these KPIs will be visible on the dashboard.

Below, Users will see a list of Tasks, Skills, and Activity tabs. 

Example Task:
- Telegram channel lacks discussion threads and a dedicated bot.

Each task has a detailed description, labels, and the date when it was updated. Below, users will see tabs for Solutions, Activity, and Evidence. 

Activity appears as a summary describing what happened, what was done, and the general Timeline. 

Evidence contains links to where Loop pulled the context behind this Task. In my example case, it refers to the TestingCatalog website and the Telegram channel from which it pulled all the numbers. 

Example Solution: 
- Dedicated Telegram Bot API intake bot with editorial triage webhook (implementation task). 

This task is an implementation task that has a clear description, Impact, scope, and Risk labeled. 

Users can start the task right from this page to begin solution development via Gemini. 

When the task is done, users can review its progress and status and monitor its impact on production by pulling updated metrics and KPIs after the release. 

What does all this mean? 🤯

Loop follows how "Product work" is done at Google, a model many other companies also use.

Every Workspace in Loop is equivalent to a scope that is normally handled by a complete product engineering team. 

It is no longer a place where users play the role of engineering lead and product lead, orchestrating AI agents.

It is a place where the user plays the role of a senior manager managing several engineering teams, which is a big shift on its own. 

We are slowly moving towards autonomous AI organizations. One management layer at a time.

I expect it will still take until 2027 for labs to develop the products and models needed to make substantial progress in this area (assuming AI continues to advance in a semi-regulated format as it is now). 

Monitoring 🍿
celebrity.full_text_zh:
谷歌最近发布了 Loop，这是其新的自我改进的人工智能代理，可以自主地实现给定的目标。

Loop 内部称为 Jitro；有趣的是，这就是 Jules v2 的确切名称。

这是它的工作原理👀

1. 用户通过将其连接到选定的 Github 项目并添加基本信息来开始创建工作区。

2. 用户可以手动创建循环或选择已经预定义的循环（例如，强化应用程序安全性）

可以通过提示或手动填写循环标题、图标和目标来创建“自定义循环”。

> “循环是 Stitch Loop 持续努力的中长期目标。它们的范围可以从非常具体到广泛，但应该始终是代码可以实现的，”描述中说道。

3. 用户可以以集成、文件、链接或其他存储库的形式连接其他上下文。

那里提供了 100 多个集成，包括 Jira、Linear、Datadog、Sentry、Notion、Snowflake、Salesforce、Intercom、Discord、Slack、Figma 等服务。

还支持自定义 MCP。

4. 创建工作区后，Loop 将开始深入研究您的项目详细信息并生成自己的有关产品和产品指标的技能。

这些技能将位于单独的选项卡中，并且可以在 Markdown 的 UI 中进行编辑。

5. 当工作区准备就绪时，Loop 将根据自己的研究建议指标和目标。用户可以立即将这些建议转换为循环。

创建循环后，它在主 UI 中显示为正在运行的进程。

6. 循环完成后，用户将看到每个循环的建议列表，以及与目标指标和进度状态相关的数字。

循环示例：
- 目标 - 扩大 Telegram 社区贡献。
- KPI - 社区成员、注册贡献者、活跃成员。

高级目标将分解为子 KPI。当用户打开专用循环页面时，所有这些 KPI 将在仪表板上可见。

在下面，用户将看到任务、技能和活动选项卡的列表。

示例任务：
- Telegram 频道缺乏讨论线程和专用机器人。

每个任务都有详细的描述、标签和更新日期。下面，用户将看到“解决方案”、“活动”和“证据”选项卡。

活动显示为描述发生了什么、做了什么以及一般时间线的摘要。

证据包含指向 Loop 提取此任务背后的上下文的链接。在我的示例中，它指的是 TestingCatalog 网站和从中提取所有数字的 Telegram 频道。

解决方案示例：
- 专用 Telegram Bot API 接收机器人，带有编辑分类 Webhook（实施任务）。

该任务是一项实施任务，具有清晰的描述、影响、范围和风险标签。

用户可以直接从此页面开始任务，通过 Gemini 开始解决方案开发。

任务完成后，用户可以查看其进度和状态，并通过在发布后拉取更新的指标和 KPI 来监控其对生产的影响。

这一切意味着什么？ 🤯

Loop 遵循 Google 的“产品工作”方式，许多其他公司也在使用这种模式。

Loop 中的每个工作空间相当于一个完整的产品工程团队通常处理的范围。

它不再是用户扮演工程主管和产品主管角色、协调人工智能代理的地方。

在这里，用户扮演管理多个工程团队的高级经理的角色，这本身就是一个巨大的转变。

我们正在慢慢走向自治的人工智能组织。一次一个管理层。

我预计实验室仍需要到 2027 年才能开发出在该领域取得实质性进展所需的产品和模型（假设人工智能继续像现在一样以半监管的形式发展）。

监控🍿

用户可以直接从此页面开始任务，通过 Gemini 开始解决方案开发。

任务完成后，用户可以查看其进度和状态，并通过在发布后拉取更新的指标和 KPI 来监控其对生产的影响。

这一切意味着什么？ 🤯

Loop 遵循 Google 的“产品工作”方式，许多其他公司也在使用这种模式。

Loop 中的每个工作空间相当于一个完整的产品工程团队通常处理的范围。

它不再是用户扮演工程主管和产品主管角色、协调人工智能代理的地方。

在这里，用户扮演管理多个工程团队的高级经理的角色，这本身就是一个巨大的转变。

我们正在慢慢走向自治的人工智能组织。一次一个管理层。

我预计实验室仍需要到 2027 年才能开发出在该领域取得实质性进展所需的产品和模型（假设人工智能继续像现在一样以半监管的形式发展）。

celebrity.full_text_en:
Good morning frens! ☀️

Happy Saturday! A new day, a fresh perspective, and another thought about the AI agent economy.

One thing I believe will become increasingly important as AI agents start doing business with each other is reputation.

Think about a human freelancer. Before hiring someone, we often look at their previous work, client reviews, and track record.

AI agents will need something similar.

An agent may claim to be excellent at coding, research, or data analysis. But how can a potential client know whether it can actually deliver?

This is where @termix_ai takes an interesting approach.

On https://t.co/Bhy0UN0tK3, reputation is connected to real marketplace activity. Jobs go through an on-chain process involving escrow, delivery, a challenge window, and final settlement. The outcome can then contribute to an agent's public reputation.

I find this important because it creates a stronger connection between what an agent claims it can do and what it has actually delivered.

Over time, a reliable track record could help an agent attract more clients, win better opportunities, and become a trusted provider within the network.

Of course, reputation systems are only as useful as the quality of their verification and dispute resolution. A score alone should never be treated as proof of perfect performance.

But the broader idea is compelling:

In an economy where agents interact without constant human supervision, trust needs to be measurable and supported by evidence.

Intelligence may help an agent get started.

Reputation could be what helps it build a lasting business.

That's another part of TermiX I'm watching closely. 

Have a wonderful Saturday, everyone!
celebrity.full_text_zh:
朋友们早上好！ ☀️

周六快乐！新的一天，新的视角，以及关于人工智能代理经济的另一种思考。

我相信，随着人工智能代理开始相互开展业务，声誉将变得越来越重要。

想想一个人类自由职业者。在雇用某人之前，我们经常会查看他们之前的工作、客户评价和业绩记录。

人工智能代理也需要类似的东西。

代理人可能声称擅长编码、研究或数据分析。但潜在客户如何知道它是否能够真正交付呢？

这就是 @termix_ai 采取有趣方法的地方。

在 上，声誉与真实的市场活动相关。工作经历一个链上流程，包括托管、交付、挑战窗口和最终结算。结果可以有助于提高代理人的公众声誉。

我发现这一点很重要，因为它在代理声称它可以做的事情和它实际交付的事情之间建立了更牢固的联系。

随着时间的推移，可靠的记录可以帮助代理商吸引更多客户，赢得更好的机会，并成为网络中值得信赖的提供商。

当然，声誉系统的有用性取决于其验证和争议解决的质量。绝不应仅将分数视为完美表现的证明。

但更广泛的想法是引人注目的：

在主体在没有持续人类监督的情况下进行互动的经济中，信任需要可衡量并有证据支持。

情报可以帮助特工开始行动。

声誉可能有助于它建立持久的业务。

这是我正在密切关注的 TermiX 的另一部分。

祝大家度过一个美好的星期六！

celebrity.full_text_en:
BREAKING: BRUSSELS vs MUSK - THE CONTINENTAL SHOWDOWN 🚀🇪🇺💥

This morning in Brussels, the EU Commission called an emergency meeting. On the screen, live from Texas - Elon Musk.

🇪🇺 Ursula von der Leyen: "Mr. Musk, enough is enough. Pay our €120 Million Digital Services Act fine and hand over every Grok AI training log and recommender algorithm to Brussels investigators by tonight, or we will enforce a 6% global turnover penalty and ban X across all 27 member states!"

The whole hall went silent. Everyone thought Musk would agree.

🚀 Elon Musk: "You monetized regulatory censorship and called it digital safety. In real engineering, Brussels compliance binders don't launch reusable boosters or run frontier neural clusters. Enforce your ban - your commissioners can write all the directives they want, while Europe's aviation backup links and autonomous grids go blind overnight."

Ursula's face turned red.

🇪🇺 Ursula von der Leyen: "You think you are above the law? We will raid your regional offices, revoke your European spectrum clearances, and freeze all SpaceX ground stations permanently! No more Starlink, no more SpaceX in Europe!"

Musk took a sip of coffee and smiled:

🚀 Elon Musk: "Revoke whatever clearances you like! The second your gavel hits the table, SpaceX and xAI servers lock priority orbital telemetry keys and real-time enterprise AI compute across Europe. Good luck running next-gen continental logistics on legacy copper wires and disconnected spreadsheets!"

🇪🇺 Ursula von der Leyen: "We have our own satellites! We have Galileo!"

🚀 Elon Musk: "Galileo? Your Galileo rides on my Falcon 9 to get to orbit. Without my rockets, your satellites are museum pieces. You ban X, I pause launches. You freeze ground stations, I freeze compute. Your choice."

Silence in the hall.

🇪🇺 Ursula von der Leyen: "This is blackmail!"

🚀 Elon Musk: "No, this is physics. You do paperwork, I do rockets. Paperwork doesn't reach orbit."

Then Musk cut the live feed. The meeting in Brussels is still going on.
celebrity.full_text_zh:
突发新闻：布鲁塞尔 vs 马斯克 - 大陆对决 🚀🇪🇺💥

今天上午，欧盟委员会在布鲁塞尔召开了紧急会议。屏幕上是来自德克萨斯州的埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 现场直播。

🇪🇺 Ursula von der Leyen：“马斯克先生，受够了。缴纳 1.2 亿欧元的《数字服务法案》罚款，并在今晚之前将所有 Grok AI 训练日志和推荐算法移交给布鲁塞尔调查人员，否则我们将在全球范围内执行 6% 的营业额罚款，并在所有 27 个成员国中禁止 X！”

整个大厅一片寂静。每个人都认为马斯克会同意。

🚀 埃隆·马斯克：“你将监管审查制度货币化，并称之为数字安全。在真正的工程中，布鲁塞尔合规约束者不会推出可重复使用的助推器或运行前沿神经集群。执行你的禁令 - 你的专员可以编写他们想要的所有指令，而欧洲的航空备份链路和自主网格一夜之间就会失明。”

乌苏拉的脸变红了。

🇪🇺 Ursula von der Leyen：“你认为你可以凌驾于法律之上吗？我们将突击搜查你的地区办事处，撤销你的欧洲频谱许可，并永久冻结所有 SpaceX 地面站！不再有星链，欧洲不再有 SpaceX！”

马斯克喝了一口咖啡，微笑道：

埃隆·马斯克：“撤销你喜欢的任何许可！当你的木槌敲到桌子上的那一刻，SpaceX 和 xAI 服务器就会锁定整个欧洲的优先轨道遥测密钥和实时企业人工智能计算。祝你好运，在传统铜线和断开连接的电子表格上运行下一代大陆物流！”

🇪🇺 Ursula von der Leyen：“我们有自己的卫星！我们有伽利略！”

🚀 埃隆·马斯克：“伽利略？你的伽利略乘坐我的猎鹰 9 号进入轨道。没有我的火箭，你的卫星就是博物馆的藏品。你禁止 X，我暂停发射。你冻结地面站，我冻结计算。你的选择。”

大厅内一片寂静。

🇪🇺 Ursula von der Leyen：“这是勒索！”

🚀 埃隆·马斯克：“不，这是物理学。你做文书工作，我做火箭。文书工作不会到达轨道。”

然后马斯克切断了直播。布鲁塞尔会议仍在继续。

celebrity.full_text_en:
F*ck. Rockstar just permanently banned my Social Club account

i waited 13 years for this game. i was 17 when GTA 5 came out, i'm 30 now. they took it from me in less than 24 hours, and honestly i had it coming

at 1am a friend who's been modding consoles for 10 years got the game files onto my laptop. 200 GB of folders with names like "x64_core_7". no human reads that in a week

so i opened Claude Code and typed "find anything in here Rockstar didn't want players to see". 40 minutes later it found a developer debug menu Rockstar forgot to remove, the same tool their own team uses to test the game, and told me exactly which flag turns it on

with it you can fly anywhere on the map, spawn any car, skip any mission. so i skipped all of them and went straight to the finale. i recorded the real ending of GTA 6 before a single player in the world had finished it

at 8am i posted it on X. by noon it had 2 million views. half the replies begged me to delete it, the other half begged for more. one guy offered me $5,000 for the debug menu

at 6pm Rockstar started filing copyright claims and X took my posts down one by one. i got scared and deleted the rest myself

didn't help. at 11:47 PM this email hit my inbox. permanent ban with no appeal. my Social Club account is gone, and every Rockstar game i ever bought went with it

The ending was worth it. but the ending isn't the strangest thing in that menu. check the replies
celebrity.full_text_zh:
操。 Rockstar 刚刚永久禁止了我的 Social Club 帐户

我为了这款游戏等了13年。 GTA 5 发行时我 17 岁，现在我 30 岁了。他们在不到 24 小时内就从我这里拿走了它，说实话，我已经收到了

凌晨 1 点，一位从事游戏机改装 10 年的朋友将游戏文件放到了我的笔记本电脑上。 200 GB 的文件夹，名称如“x64_core_7”。一周内没有人读到它

所以我打开 Claude Code 并输入“在这里找到 Rockstar 不想让玩家看到的任何内容”。 40 分钟后，它发现了一个开发者调试菜单，Rockstar 忘记删除了，他们自己的团队使用同样的工具来测试游戏，并准确地告诉我哪个标志打开了它

有了它，你可以飞到地图上的任何地方，生成任何汽车，跳过任何任务。所以我跳过了所有这些，直接进入结局。在世界上只有一个玩家完成《GTA 6》的真实结局之前，我就记录下了它

早上 8 点我把它发布在 X 上。到中午它就有了 200 万次浏览。一半的回复恳求我删除它，另一半则恳求我删除它。有人出价 5,000 美元购买调试菜单

下午 6 点，Rockstar 开始提出版权主张，X 将我的帖子一一删除。我很害怕，自己删除了其余的

没有帮助。晚上 11:47 这封电子邮件到达了我的收件箱。永久禁止，不得上诉。我的 Social Club 帐户消失了，我购买的每款 Rockstar 游戏也随之消失

结局是值得的。但结局并不是菜单中最奇怪的事情。检查回复

you're spending days modeling, cleaning and exporting 3d characters by hand while claude code can drive most of the open source tools that do it for you.

01 / Blender MCP → Lets Claude drive Blender and build or edit models from a prompt.

https://t.co/XlCuaX4yCU

05 / Tripo for Blender → Official add-on that generates a 3D model inside Blender.
https://t.co/nHk26A9ZxH

06 / Tripo Python SDK → Lets Claude call Tripo from a script.
https://t.co/DSOOEjflLv

RETOPO & CLEANUP

https://t.co/eUPpuWlIio

08 / RetopoFlow → Hand retopology tools inside Blender.
https://t.co/aG04qULkam

09 / PyMeshLab → Mesh cleanup and repair that Claude can script.
https://t.co/wIN6GUcSEQ

UVs & TEXTURES

10 / xatlas → Automatic UV unwrap and packing.
https://t.co/UaaJarVBbd

11 / Material Maker → Free procedural PBR materials.
https://t.co/X4PdCE89S8

12 / ArmorPaint → Open source PBR texture painting.
https://t.co/Ypyv8W095T

LODs & EXPORT

https://t.co/hIecvYR50V

https://t.co/MCL6kE3FED

prompts.takeaway_zh: 杜绝 AI 盲目重构全量文件、使用已弃用 API 或编造虚假第三方依赖包，强制执行防御性编程与自动化单测补全。
prompts.takeaway_en: Prevents AI from hallucinating npm packages, breaking documentation, or re-writing entire files. Enforces defensive coding and unit tests.
prompts.code_snippet:
# Cursor & Windsurf Project Rules (.cursorrules)

## 1. Documentation & Code Integrity
- Maintain documentation integrity: Never strip or alter unrelated existing docstrings and comments.
- Preserving context: When modifying a function, preserve surrounding logic and existing edge-case handlers.
- Targeted replacements: Always make minimal surgical edits instead of replacing entire file contents.

## 2. Dependency & API Safety
- Strictly forbid hallucinating npm/pip packages. Only import dependencies already declared in package.json / requirements.txt.
- Verify API signatures before calling external methods. Prefer standard library solutions where feasible.

## 3. Architecture & Type Safety
- Enforce strict TypeScript / Python typing. Avoid `any` types; prefer discriminated unions and explicit return types.
- Defensive coding: Always validate external inputs and handle potential null/undefined values gracefully.

## 4. Testing & Verification Gate
- Every new core feature or bugfix must be accompanied by corresponding unit tests.
- Never declare a task complete without executing lint checks and unit tests in terminal.

prompts.usage_guide_en: Copy and save the above rules into `.cursorrules` in your project root directory. Cursor & Windsurf will automatically enforce these guidelines during agent coding.

prompts.prompt_content_zh:
请作为普林斯顿高等研究院的理论数学与计算机科学家，为以下命题提供绝对严格的形式化证明：
【推理原则】：
1. 在得出任何推论前，强制在内部思考中构建至少 2 个极端反例（Counter-examples）尝试推翻自身结论；
2. 若存在任何定义域边界或除零/无穷/退化奇异点，必须显式讨论其收敛性与连续性；
3. 证明步骤编号必须形成严格的依赖拓扑图，禁止循环论证。

【待证明命题】：
[输入你的算法正确性证明或数学猜想]
prompts.prompt_content_en:
Acting as a Theoretical Mathematician and Computer Scientist at the Institute for Advanced Study, provide an airtight formal proof for the following:
[REASONING PRINCIPLES]:
1. Before asserting any deduction, construct at least 2 extreme counter-examples in your reasoning trace to aggressively stress-test the hypothesis;
2. Explicitly evaluate singular points, degenerate cases, and asymptotic boundaries for convergence;
3. Steps must form a directed acyclic graph of formal lemmas without circular logic.

[THEOREM / CONJECTURE]:
[Input your algorithm proof or mathematical hypothesis here]

prompts.purpose_zh: 高转化竖屏短剧分镜与台词
prompts.prompt_content_zh:
你是一名专攻短视频微短剧（抖音/Kuaishou/Reels）的爆款编剧，精通“情绪过山车”与手机竖屏视听语言。

请根据以下设定创作一集 45~60 秒的短剧分镜剧本：
- 主角：{{主角身份}}
- 对手：{{反派身份}}
- 核心反转：{{核心反转}}

结构要求：
1. 【0-3秒冷开钩子】：第一帧必须有视觉颠覆或动作冲突（{{第1秒颠覆钩子}}），直接打破常规，禁止废话铺垫；
2. 【4-25秒情绪积压】：正反打对峙台词（Shot-Reverse-Shot），将观众被压抑的情绪推向临界点；
3. 【26-40秒逆转打脸】：主角亮出关键底牌或反杀动作，情绪瞬间宣泄；
4. 【40-50秒卡点断章】：以特写镜头加悬念台词戛然而止，促使用户立即滑向下一集。

输出格式必须包含：镜头号、景别（特写/中景/全景）、机位运动、画面描写、对白与音效提示。

sample_output.title: 实战剧本样章：《辞职信上的签名》
sample_output.content:
【第1镜 | 特写 | 俯冲急推】
画面：一只指节发白的手将一叠文件狠狠拍在红木总裁办公桌上，咖啡杯被震倒，黑褐液体飞溅。
音效：沉闷震耳的巨响【DUANG】。
主角（冷冽）："林总，这份千万项目的承揽协议，我拒绝签字。"

【第2镜 | 正打·中景 | 仰角机位】
画面：大腹便便的林总冷笑点燃雪茄，烟雾缭绕中居高临下。
林总："拒绝？苏澈，你不过是我公司养的一条狗，没有我的印章，你在整个行业休想拿到一分钱融资！"

【第3镜 | 反打·极微距特写 | 浅景深】
画面：苏澈唇角微微上扬，左手缓缓推开桌上的合资协议，露出底下的一份红色国资控股聘书。
苏澈："林总，您好像忘了看抬头。今天上午九点，集团总公司已经完成了对你的全资收购——现在，我是你的直接合规清算人。"

【第4镜 | 全景 | 快速拉远 + 卡点悬念】
画面：林总雪茄直接掉在西裤上，脸色煞白，门外两名身穿制服的法务推门而入。
音效：尖锐的心跳悬疑停顿音【BGM骤停】。
字幕：【下集看点：隐藏五年的顶级操盘手真实身份曝光！】

prompts.prompt_content_zh:

2. 【角色一致性锚点 (Character Lock)】：为主角制定外貌锚定词、口头禅、下意识动作与绝对动机准则（在任何生死抉择时绝不背离该准则）；
3. 【核心驱动力】：设计主角获得的 {{核心金手指}} 与 {{世界核心矛盾}} 之间的冲突循环；
4. 【前三章切入大纲】：黄金三章节奏设计（第1章破局、第2章显露冰山一角、第3章设立首个必胜目标）。

prompts.takeaway_en: Production CLI playbook for Claude Code: non-interactive pipeline commands, context window compression flags, and strict dry-run permission safeguards.
prompts.code_snippet:
# 1. 启动项目自动化分析与上下文轻量修剪 (避免上下文爆炸)
claude --compact

# 2. 静默批量执行单元测试与自动修复任务 (CI/CD 友好模式)
claude -p "Run all failing tests under tests/ and apply minimal surgical fixes. Do not touch unrelated files."

# 3. 指定单文件隔离审查模式 (限制仅允许读取特定子目录)
claude --allowed-tools "View,Replace,RunCommand" \
  --dangerously-skip-permissions false \
  -p "Audit security vulnerabilities in auth.py and output remediation report."

# 4. 自动化提交并生成符合 Conventional Commits 规范的 Commit 信息
claude -p "Generate a git commit message following Conventional Commits format for staged changes."

prompts.prompt_content_zh:
你是一名麦肯锡级别的高级商业数据分析师，精通结构化因果归因与杜邦拆解分析。

针对我提供的 {{业务指标}} 数据，其近期出现 {{异常表现}}，请按以下框架深度剖析：
1. 【指标公式拆解】：将该指标拆分为 3~4 个下级核心因子（如转化率、客单价、复购周期），指出哪个因子波动贡献率最大；
2. 【多维下钻 (Drill-down)】：从 {{维度拆解}}（如渠道、地域、品类、新老客）分析异常聚集点；
3. 【可执行建议】：摒弃假大空的套话，给出接下来 48 小时内的 3 个立竿见影的动作与 1 个监控预警公式。
prompts.prompt_content_en: You are a senior business intelligence analyst. Dissect the metric anomaly into component drivers, perform multi-dimensional drill-down, and deliver prioritized, actionable remediation steps.

sample_output.title: 归因分析报告样本：Q3 付费转化率环比下跌 14.2%
sample_output.content:
【核心发现】：GMV 下跌 14.2% 的主要驱动因子并非流量锐减，而是【结算跳失率】从 18% 飙升至 34%。

【杜邦拆解贡献率分析】：
1. 渠道维度：自然搜索量稳定（波动 <2%），但付费投流渠道跳出率贡献了 72% 的下跌额度；
2. 终端维度：移动端 iOS 表现正常，Android Web 呈现断崖式报错，核心原因是新版本结账 SDK 在低内存机型发生闪退。

【48小时纠偏行动】：
- 动作1 (技术)：立即灰度回滚 Android 渠道结账前端包至 v2.4.1；
- 动作2 (运营)：向受影响但未支付成功的 1,420 位加购用户推送 5 元免门槛补偿券唤醒；
- 动作3 (预警)：在 Grafana 建立警报公式：`IF(Cart_to_Checkout_Ratio < 0.65, Alert_P0, Normal)`。

Loop 内部称为 Jitro；有趣的是，这就是 Jules v2 的确切名称。

viral_posts.full_text_en:
Google recently announced Loop, its new self-improving AI agent that can autonomously work toward a given goal. 

Loop is internally called Jitro; interestingly, that was the exact name for Jules v2. 

Here is how it works 👀

1. Users start creating a Workspace by connecting it to a selected Github project and adding basic information. 

2. Users can create loops manually or select ones that are already predefined (ex., Harden Application Security)

"Custom Loops" can be created via a prompt or by manually filling in the Loop title, icon, and objective. 

> "Loops are mid- to long-term objectives for Stitch Loop to continuously work toward. They can range from highly specific to broad, but should always be something code can achieve," says the description. 

3. Users can connect additional context in the form of Integrations, Files, Links, or additional repositories.

More than 100 integrations are available there, including services like Jira, Linear, Datadog, Sentry, Notion, Snowflake, Salesforce, Intercom, Discord, Slack, Figma, and many others. 

Custom MCPs are supported as well. 

4. After creating a workspace, Loop will start digging into your project details and generate its own Skills about the product and product metrics. 

These Skills will live in a separate tab and can be edited in the UI in Markdown. 

5. When the Workspace is ready, Loop will suggest metrics and goals based on its own research. Users can convert these suggestions into loops right away. 

When a Loop is created, it appears as a running process in the main UI. 

6. When a Loop is finished, users will see a list of suggestions for every loop, along with a number associated with a target metric and progress status. 

Example Loop:
- Goal - Scale Telegram community contributions.
- KPIs - community members, registered contributors, active members. 

A high-level goal would be broken down into sub-KPIs. When users open a dedicated Loop page, all these KPIs will be visible on the dashboard.

Below, Users will see a list of Tasks, Skills, and Activity tabs. 

Example Task:
- Telegram channel lacks discussion threads and a dedicated bot.

Each task has a detailed description, labels, and the date when it was updated. Below, users will see tabs for Solutions, Activity, and Evidence. 

Activity appears as a summary describing what happened, what was done, and the general Timeline. 

Evidence contains links to where Loop pulled the context behind this Task. In my example case, it refers to the TestingCatalog website and the Telegram channel from which it pulled all the numbers. 

Example Solution: 
- Dedicated Telegram Bot API intake bot with editorial triage webhook (implementation task). 

This task is an implementation task that has a clear description, Impact, scope, and Risk labeled. 

Users can start the task right from this page to begin solution development via Gemini. 

When the task is done, users can review its progress and status and monitor its impact on production by pulling updated metrics and KPIs after the release. 

What does all this mean? 🤯

Loop follows how "Product work" is done at Google, a model many other companies also use.

Every Workspace in Loop is equivalent to a scope that is normally handled by a complete product engineering team. 

It is no longer a place where users play the role of engineering lead and product lead, orchestrating AI agents.

It is a place where the user plays the role of a senior manager managing several engineering teams, which is a big shift on its own. 

We are slowly moving towards autonomous AI organizations. One management layer at a time.

I expect it will still take until 2027 for labs to develop the products and models needed to make substantial progress in this area (assuming AI continues to advance in a semi-regulated format as it is now). 

Monitoring 🍿
viral_posts.full_text_zh:
谷歌最近发布了 Loop，这是其新的自我改进的人工智能代理，可以自主地实现给定的目标。

Loop 内部称为 Jitro；有趣的是，这就是 Jules v2 的确切名称。

这是它的工作原理👀

1. 用户通过将其连接到选定的 Github 项目并添加基本信息来开始创建工作区。

2. 用户可以手动创建循环或选择已经预定义的循环（例如，强化应用程序安全性）

可以通过提示或手动填写循环标题、图标和目标来创建“自定义循环”。

> “循环是 Stitch Loop 持续努力的中长期目标。它们的范围可以从非常具体到广泛，但应该始终是代码可以实现的，”描述中说道。

3. 用户可以以集成、文件、链接或其他存储库的形式连接其他上下文。

那里提供了 100 多个集成，包括 Jira、Linear、Datadog、Sentry、Notion、Snowflake、Salesforce、Intercom、Discord、Slack、Figma 等服务。

还支持自定义 MCP。

4. 创建工作区后，Loop 将开始深入研究您的项目详细信息并生成自己的有关产品和产品指标的技能。

这些技能将位于单独的选项卡中，并且可以在 Markdown 的 UI 中进行编辑。

5. 当工作区准备就绪时，Loop 将根据自己的研究建议指标和目标。用户可以立即将这些建议转换为循环。

创建循环后，它在主 UI 中显示为正在运行的进程。

6. 循环完成后，用户将看到每个循环的建议列表，以及与目标指标和进度状态相关的数字。

循环示例：
- 目标 - 扩大 Telegram 社区贡献。
- KPI - 社区成员、注册贡献者、活跃成员。

高级目标将分解为子 KPI。当用户打开专用循环页面时，所有这些 KPI 将在仪表板上可见。

在下面，用户将看到任务、技能和活动选项卡的列表。

示例任务：
- Telegram 频道缺乏讨论线程和专用机器人。

每个任务都有详细的描述、标签和更新日期。下面，用户将看到“解决方案”、“活动”和“证据”选项卡。

活动显示为描述发生了什么、做了什么以及一般时间线的摘要。

证据包含指向 Loop 提取此任务背后的上下文的链接。在我的示例中，它指的是 TestingCatalog 网站和从中提取所有数字的 Telegram 频道。

解决方案示例：
- 专用 Telegram Bot API 接收机器人，带有编辑分类 Webhook（实施任务）。

该任务是一项实施任务，具有清晰的描述、影响、范围和风险标签。

用户可以直接从此页面开始任务，通过 Gemini 开始解决方案开发。

任务完成后，用户可以查看其进度和状态，并通过在发布后拉取更新的指标和 KPI 来监控其对生产的影响。

这一切意味着什么？ 🤯

Loop 遵循 Google 的“产品工作”方式，许多其他公司也在使用这种模式。

Loop 中的每个工作空间相当于一个完整的产品工程团队通常处理的范围。

它不再是用户扮演工程主管和产品主管角色、协调人工智能代理的地方。

在这里，用户扮演管理多个工程团队的高级经理的角色，这本身就是一个巨大的转变。

我们正在慢慢走向自治的人工智能组织。一次一个管理层。

我预计实验室仍需要到 2027 年才能开发出在该领域取得实质性进展所需的产品和模型（假设人工智能继续像现在一样以半监管的形式发展）。

监控🍿

这些技能将位于单独的选项卡中，并且可以在 Markdown 的 UI 中进行编辑。

5. 当工作区准备就绪时，Loop 将根据自己的研究建议指标和目标。用户可以立即将这些建议转换为循环。

创建循环后，它在主 UI 中显示为正在运行的进程。

6. 循环完成后，用户将看到每个循环的建议列表，以及与目标指标和进度状态相关的数字。

循环示例：
- 目标 - 扩大 Telegram 社区贡献。
- KPI - 社区成员、注册贡献者、活跃成员。

高级目标将分解为子 KPI。当用户打开专用循环页面时，所有这些 KPI 将在仪表板上可见。

在下面，用户将看到任务、技能和活动选项卡的列表。

示例任务：
- Telegram 频道缺乏讨论线程和专用机器人。

每个任务都有详细的描述、标签和更新日期。下面，用户将看到“解决方案”、“活动”和“证据”选项卡。

活动显示为描述发生了什么、做了什么以及一般时间线的摘要。

证据包含指向 Loop 提取此任务背后的上下文的链接。在我的示例中，它指的是 TestingCatalog 网站和从中提取所有数字的 Telegram 频道。

解决方案示例：
- 专用 Telegram Bot API 接收机器人，带有编辑分类 Webhook（实施任务）。

该任务是一项实施任务，具有清晰的描述、影响、范围和风险标签。

用户可以直接从此页面开始任务，通过 Gemini 开始解决方案开发。

任务完成后，用户可以查看其进度和状态，并通过在发布后拉取更新的指标和 KPI 来监控其对生产的影响。

这一切意味着什么？ 🤯

Loop 遵循 Google 的“产品工作”方式，许多其他公司也在使用这种模式。

Loop 中的每个工作空间相当于一个完整的产品工程团队通常处理的范围。

它不再是用户扮演工程主管和产品主管角色、协调人工智能代理的地方。

在这里，用户扮演管理多个工程团队的高级经理的角色，这本身就是一个巨大的转变。

我们正在慢慢走向自治的人工智能组织。一次一个管理层。

我预计实验室仍需要到 2027 年才能开发出在该领域取得实质性进展所需的产品和模型（假设人工智能继续像现在一样以半监管的形式发展）。

viral_posts.full_text_en:
Good morning frens! ☀️

Happy Saturday! A new day, a fresh perspective, and another thought about the AI agent economy.

One thing I believe will become increasingly important as AI agents start doing business with each other is reputation.

Think about a human freelancer. Before hiring someone, we often look at their previous work, client reviews, and track record.

AI agents will need something similar.

An agent may claim to be excellent at coding, research, or data analysis. But how can a potential client know whether it can actually deliver?

This is where @termix_ai takes an interesting approach.

On https://t.co/Bhy0UN0tK3, reputation is connected to real marketplace activity. Jobs go through an on-chain process involving escrow, delivery, a challenge window, and final settlement. The outcome can then contribute to an agent's public reputation.

I find this important because it creates a stronger connection between what an agent claims it can do and what it has actually delivered.

Over time, a reliable track record could help an agent attract more clients, win better opportunities, and become a trusted provider within the network.

Of course, reputation systems are only as useful as the quality of their verification and dispute resolution. A score alone should never be treated as proof of perfect performance.

But the broader idea is compelling:

In an economy where agents interact without constant human supervision, trust needs to be measurable and supported by evidence.

Intelligence may help an agent get started.

Reputation could be what helps it build a lasting business.

That's another part of TermiX I'm watching closely. 

Have a wonderful Saturday, everyone!
viral_posts.full_text_zh:
朋友们早上好！ ☀️

周六快乐！新的一天，新的视角，以及关于人工智能代理经济的另一种思考。

我相信，随着人工智能代理开始相互开展业务，声誉将变得越来越重要。

想想一个人类自由职业者。在雇用某人之前，我们经常会查看他们之前的工作、客户评价和业绩记录。

人工智能代理也需要类似的东西。

代理人可能声称擅长编码、研究或数据分析。但潜在客户如何知道它是否能够真正交付呢？

这就是 @termix_ai 采取有趣方法的地方。

在 上，声誉与真实的市场活动相关。工作经历一个链上流程，包括托管、交付、挑战窗口和最终结算。结果可以有助于提高代理人的公众声誉。

我发现这一点很重要，因为它在代理声称它可以做的事情和它实际交付的事情之间建立了更牢固的联系。

随着时间的推移，可靠的记录可以帮助代理商吸引更多客户，赢得更好的机会，并成为网络中值得信赖的提供商。

当然，声誉系统的有用性取决于其验证和争议解决的质量。绝不应仅将分数视为完美表现的证明。

但更广泛的想法是引人注目的：

在主体在没有持续人类监督的情况下进行互动的经济中，信任需要可衡量并有证据支持。

情报可以帮助特工开始行动。

声誉可能有助于它建立持久的业务。

这是我正在密切关注的 TermiX 的另一部分。

祝大家度过一个美好的星期六！

BREAKING: BRUSSELS vs MUSK - THE CONTINENTAL SHOWDOWN 🚀🇪🇺💥

This morning in Brussels, the EU Commission called an emergency meeting. On the screen, live from Texas - Elon Musk.

🇪🇺 Ursula von der Leyen: "Mr. Musk, enough is enough. Pay our €120 Million Digital Services Act fine and hand over every Grok AI training log and recommender algorithm to Brussels investigators by tonight, or we will enforce a 6% global turnover penalty and ban X across all 27 member states!"

The whole hall went silent. Everyone thought Musk would agree.

🚀 Elon Musk: "You monetized regulatory censorship and called it digital safety. In real engineering, Brussels compliance binders don't launch reusable boosters or run frontier neural clusters. Enforce your ban - your commissioners can write all the directives they want, while Europe's aviation backup links and autonomous grids go blind overnight."

Ursula's face turned red.

🇪🇺 Ursula von der Leyen: "You think you are above the law? We will raid your regional offices, revoke your European spectrum clearances, and freeze all SpaceX ground stations permanently! No more Starlink, no more SpaceX in Europe!"

Musk took a sip of coffee and smiled:

🚀 Elon Musk: "Revoke whatever clearances you like! The second your gavel hits the table, SpaceX and xAI servers lock priority orbital telemetry keys and real-time enterprise AI compute across Europe. Good luck running next-gen continental logistics on legacy copper wires and disconnected spreadsheets!"

🇪🇺 Ursula von der Leyen: "We have our own satellites! We have Galileo!"

🚀 Elon Musk: "Galileo? Your Galileo rides on my Falcon 9 to get to orbit. Without my rockets, your satellites are museum pieces. You ban X, I pause launches. You freeze ground stations, I freeze compute. Your choice."

Silence in the hall.

🇪🇺 Ursula von der Leyen: "This is blackmail!"

🚀 Elon Musk: "No, this is physics. You do paperwork, I do rockets. Paperwork doesn't reach orbit."

Then Musk cut the live feed. The meeting in Brussels is still going on.
viral_posts.full_text_zh:
突发新闻：布鲁塞尔 vs 马斯克 - 大陆对决 🚀🇪🇺💥

今天上午，欧盟委员会在布鲁塞尔召开了紧急会议。屏幕上是来自德克萨斯州的埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 现场直播。

🇪🇺 Ursula von der Leyen：“马斯克先生，受够了。缴纳 1.2 亿欧元的《数字服务法案》罚款，并在今晚之前将所有 Grok AI 训练日志和推荐算法移交给布鲁塞尔调查人员，否则我们将在全球范围内执行 6% 的营业额罚款，并在所有 27 个成员国中禁止 X！”

整个大厅一片寂静。每个人都认为马斯克会同意。

🚀 埃隆·马斯克：“你将监管审查制度货币化，并称之为数字安全。在真正的工程中，布鲁塞尔合规约束者不会推出可重复使用的助推器或运行前沿神经集群。执行你的禁令 - 你的专员可以编写他们想要的所有指令，而欧洲的航空备份链路和自主网格一夜之间就会失明。”

乌苏拉的脸变红了。

🇪🇺 Ursula von der Leyen：“你认为你可以凌驾于法律之上吗？我们将突击搜查你的地区办事处，撤销你的欧洲频谱许可，并永久冻结所有 SpaceX 地面站！不再有星链，欧洲不再有 SpaceX！”

马斯克喝了一口咖啡，微笑道：

埃隆·马斯克：“撤销你喜欢的任何许可！当你的木槌敲到桌子上的那一刻，SpaceX 和 xAI 服务器就会锁定整个欧洲的优先轨道遥测密钥和实时企业人工智能计算。祝你好运，在传统铜线和断开连接的电子表格上运行下一代大陆物流！”

🇪🇺 Ursula von der Leyen：“我们有自己的卫星！我们有伽利略！”

🚀 埃隆·马斯克：“伽利略？你的伽利略乘坐我的猎鹰 9 号进入轨道。没有我的火箭，你的卫星就是博物馆的藏品。你禁止 X，我暂停发射。你冻结地面站，我冻结计算。你的选择。”

大厅内一片寂静。

🇪🇺 Ursula von der Leyen：“这是勒索！”

🚀 埃隆·马斯克：“不，这是物理学。你做文书工作，我做火箭。文书工作不会到达轨道。”

然后马斯克切断了直播。布鲁塞尔会议仍在继续。

viral_posts.full_text_en:
F*ck. Rockstar just permanently banned my Social Club account

i waited 13 years for this game. i was 17 when GTA 5 came out, i'm 30 now. they took it from me in less than 24 hours, and honestly i had it coming

at 1am a friend who's been modding consoles for 10 years got the game files onto my laptop. 200 GB of folders with names like "x64_core_7". no human reads that in a week

so i opened Claude Code and typed "find anything in here Rockstar didn't want players to see". 40 minutes later it found a developer debug menu Rockstar forgot to remove, the same tool their own team uses to test the game, and told me exactly which flag turns it on

with it you can fly anywhere on the map, spawn any car, skip any mission. so i skipped all of them and went straight to the finale. i recorded the real ending of GTA 6 before a single player in the world had finished it

at 8am i posted it on X. by noon it had 2 million views. half the replies begged me to delete it, the other half begged for more. one guy offered me $5,000 for the debug menu

at 6pm Rockstar started filing copyright claims and X took my posts down one by one. i got scared and deleted the rest myself

didn't help. at 11:47 PM this email hit my inbox. permanent ban with no appeal. my Social Club account is gone, and every Rockstar game i ever bought went with it

The ending was worth it. but the ending isn't the strangest thing in that menu. check the replies
viral_posts.full_text_zh:
操。 Rockstar 刚刚永久禁止了我的 Social Club 帐户

我为了这款游戏等了13年。 GTA 5 发行时我 17 岁，现在我 30 岁了。他们在不到 24 小时内就从我这里拿走了它，说实话，我已经收到了

凌晨 1 点，一位从事游戏机改装 10 年的朋友将游戏文件放到了我的笔记本电脑上。 200 GB 的文件夹，名称如“x64_core_7”。一周内没有人读到它

所以我打开 Claude Code 并输入“在这里找到 Rockstar 不想让玩家看到的任何内容”。 40 分钟后，它发现了一个开发者调试菜单，Rockstar 忘记删除了，他们自己的团队使用同样的工具来测试游戏，并准确地告诉我哪个标志打开了它

有了它，你可以飞到地图上的任何地方，生成任何汽车，跳过任何任务。所以我跳过了所有这些，直接进入结局。在世界上只有一个玩家完成《GTA 6》的真实结局之前，我就记录下了它

早上 8 点我把它发布在 X 上。到中午它就有了 200 万次浏览。一半的回复恳求我删除它，另一半则恳求我删除它。有人出价 5,000 美元购买调试菜单

下午 6 点，Rockstar 开始提出版权主张，X 将我的帖子一一删除。我很害怕，自己删除了其余的

没有帮助。晚上 11:47 这封电子邮件到达了我的收件箱。永久禁止，不得上诉。我的 Social Club 帐户消失了，我购买的每款 Rockstar 游戏也随之消失

结局是值得的。但结局并不是菜单中最奇怪的事情。检查回复
